newsitem.title: INDIA: India RBI cuts interest cap on 1 yr deposits.
newsitem.headline: India RBI cuts interest cap on 1 yr deposits.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) said on Saturday it cut the interest cap on bank deposits up to one year to 10 percent from 11 percent.

"It has been decided to reduce effective from October 21, 1996, the deposit rates for maturity of 30 days and upto one year by one percentage point from 'not exceeding 11.0 percent per annum' to 'not exceeding 10.0 percent per annum,'" it said.
It said banks should continue to obtain the prior approval of their respective boards for the deposit rates they will be offering on deposits of maturity of over one year.
"At any point of time, individual banks should adopt uniform rates at all their branches and for all customers."

At present, interest rates on domestic term deposits of scheduled commercial banks (excluding regional rural banks) are subject to a prescription of 'not exceeding 11.0 percent per annum for maturity of 30 days and upto one year.
For maturity of over one year, banks are free to fix their own interest rates.
